description: Common kingfisher (Alcedo atthis): perches over water, takes off to fish prey it has seen, eats it on a perch, roosts in cover at night and flees a threat by flight. Written for Alcedo atthis because the shared perching-songbird program adds song, hopping foraging and cup nesting, and the shared seabird program walks to prey. The perch-and-sally structure follows the species-local tyrannus-forficatus program. Representation limit: the plunge dive into water is not modelled; the animal flies to the prey and eats it. No nesting branch is included because a burrow excavation action does not exist, so no nesting months are enabled. No song or call branch is included because the species has no song.
